title: Lebanon is trying to make trade and investment policy answerable to employment through evidence, sector selection, and tripartite coordination
source_unit: ILO report on the launch of the Mainstreaming Employment into Trade and Investment (METI) project in Lebanon, published 27 August 2026
geography: Lebanon, with regional Southern Mediterranean METI II connections across Algeria, Egypt, Jordan, Lebanon, Libya, Morocco, Palestine, Syria, and Tunisia

observations.period: August 2026 onward; Lebanon METI project launch and policy-working-group formation

denominator.unit: national employment-centred trade and investment project in Lebanon

project.value: Mainstreaming Employment into Trade and Investment (METI) project

funder.value: European Union funding with ILO implementation

policy_working_group.value: a Policy Working Group was established with labour, economy and trade, industry, employer, worker, and research representatives

policy_problem.value: trade, investment, and employment policies do not automatically produce more or better jobs when designed separately

observations.method: Official ILO report of project launch, stakeholder composition, and planned policy-analysis approach; it is an institutional announcement, not an impact evaluation.
observations.uncertainty: The launch does not establish that the working group will influence policy, that stakeholders have equal power, or that later interventions will create jobs or improve job quality.
observations.subgroup: Lebanese ministries, employers, worker organizations, researchers, firms, workers, young people, women, MSMEs, and households affected by economic recovery.
observations.counterinterpretation: A policy working group can remain consultative, fragmented, or dominated by better-resourced institutions; coordination does not guarantee implementation, finance, or worker remedy.

denominator.unit: planned Lebanon sector-selection and employment-action route

sector_selection.value: the project will identify a priority export-oriented sector or value chain with employment potential

action_plan.value: national stakeholders will support a sectoral action plan addressing trade, investment, and employment angles

analysis_tools.value: policy analysis, sector selection, value-chain analysis, employment-potential assessment, and impact assessment are planned tools

employment_goal.value: translate trade and investment opportunities into productive employment and decent work

observations.method: ILO description of METI's planned analytical and participatory methods and sectoral implementation route.
observations.uncertainty: The project has not yet demonstrated which sector will be selected, what baseline employment effects exist, or whether a plan will be financed, implemented, evaluated, and enforced.
observations.subgroup: Export-oriented firms, MSMEs, workers, women and youth, suppliers, sector institutions, investors, policymakers, and communities dependent on selected value chains.
observations.counterinterpretation: Selecting sectors for export potential can privilege internationally competitive firms or formal workers while overlooking domestic services, informal livelihoods, care work, or regions with weaker market access.

observations.period: 2026–2028; firm, worker, skills, gender, and formalization route

denominator.unit: planned targeted-intervention package for selected export-oriented activities

enterprise_support.value: targeted measures will support micro, small, and medium-sized enterprises and workers

skills.value: skills development will be supported where gaps are identified in selected export-oriented activities

inclusion.value: analysis and interventions will integrate employment quality, skills needs, gender equality, and formalization

target_groups.value: particular attention will be given to women and young people

observations.method: ILO project design description of planned firm, worker, skills, gender, and formalization measures.
observations.uncertainty: The design does not establish who will receive support, whether skills match employer demand, or whether formalization improves protection rather than raising entry barriers.
observations.subgroup: Women, youth, MSMEs, informal workers, export workers, suppliers, employers, training providers, and households with limited labour-market room.
observations.counterinterpretation: Skills programmes can shift responsibility to workers, and formalization can exclude firms or workers if compliance costs exceed support; export growth can also intensify work or environmental pressures.

denominator.unit: countries named in the wider Southern Mediterranean METI programme geography

regional_countries.value: Algeria, Egypt, Jordan, Lebanon, Libya, Morocco, Palestine, Syria, and Tunisia

regional_exchange.value: policymakers and social partners will exchange knowledge, good practices, and potential regional value-chain linkages

regional_goals.value: market diversification, value-chain upgrading, economic resilience, employment, and social inclusion

geopolitical_mechanism.value: EU-backed regional cooperation uses employment-centred policy analysis to connect trade integration, national recovery, and decent work

observations.method: ILO account of Lebanon's participation in METI II and the programme's Southern Mediterranean regional dimension.
observations.uncertainty: Regional exchange and integration do not establish convergence, shared bargaining power, cross-border job gains, or equitable distribution across countries and value chains.
observations.subgroup: Southern Mediterranean governments, social partners, firms, workers, women, youth, MSMEs, investors, and communities affected by regional value chains.
observations.counterinterpretation: Regional integration can expand opportunity for connected firms while increasing competition, labour arbitrage, migration pressure, or uneven exposure for weaker regions and workers.

related_sources.claim: ILO METI programme page describing the Southern Mediterranean regional programme and methods.
Complementary ILO Lebanon cooperative-data and rural-livelihood partnership.

boundary: This record adds a policy-design route linking trade and investment, employment measurement, tripartite coordination, export-oriented value chains, MSMEs, skills, gender, formalization, regional integration, and inclusive recovery. It records a project launch and planned mechanisms, not actual trade growth, job creation, wage change, firm performance, worker outcomes, or implemented policy effects.
